title: Storage Queues and Timer Triggers
description: Use Queue and Timer triggers in Azure Functions for background processing and scheduled tasks.

data.text: Two of the most useful triggers in Azure Functions are Queue triggers (for processing background messages) and Timer triggers (for scheduled jobs). They work together to decouple workloads and automate repetitive tasks.
A Queue trigger fires when a new message arrives in an Azure Storage Queue. This is ideal for background processing where you want to decouple the sender from the processor.

items: Automatically polls the queue for new messages
Supports poison message handling (dead-letter queue after failures)
Function receives the message content as a parameter

data.title: C# — Queue Trigger Function

data.text: Timer triggers use CRON expressions to run on a schedule. The timer trigger guarantees that the function does not run again until the previous instance completes.

data.title: CRON Expression Format
data.text: Azure Functions uses NCRONTAB format: `{second} {minute} {hour} {day} {month} {day-of-week}`. The expression '0 0 */6 * * *' runs every 6 hours on the hour.

terms.definition: A trigger that starts a function when a message is added to an Azure Storage Queue.
A message that repeatedly fails processing; Azure moves it to a dead-letter queue after max retries.
A time-based schedule string used by Timer triggers to define when a function runs.

data.expectedOutcome: The function logs each message from the queue as it is processed.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Queue triggers process messages from Azure Storage Queues
Timer triggers run on a CRON schedule
Both triggers support retry and error handling
data.takeaway: Queue and Timer triggers are the backbone of background and scheduled Azure Functions.
